steps.title: Grow Plant Material
steps.instruction: Grow Arabidopsis or wheat under a 12-hour photoperiod at 21 °C and 50% relative humidity, with approx. 100 µmol photons m-2 s-1 light intensity on soil (Premium potting mix, Martins fertilizers) supplemented with fertiliser (1 g/kg Osmocote).

substeps.instruction: For Arabidopsis: grow for 3 weeks on soil or 1-2 weeks on nutrient-rich media (half-strength Gamborg B5 or Murashige Skoog media supplemented with 1% sucrose).
For wheat: grow for 1 week on soil.
Ensure plants are stress-free from droughts, pathogens, and pests.

steps.title: Prepare Digestion Enzyme Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare 10 mL of digestion medium based on the species-specific composition.

substeps.instruction: Combine 100 mM MES-KOH (pH 5.7) [2 mL], 1 M Mannitol [6 mL], 100 mM KCl [2 mL for Arabidopsis; 1 mL for wheat], and dd-water [800 uL].
Add enzymes: Cellulase R-10 [150 mg for Arabidopsis] or Cellulase RS [150 mg for wheat], and Macerozyme R-10 [40 mg for Arabidopsis; 75 mg for wheat].
Warm the solution to 55 °C for 10 min with occasional swirling to inactivate nucleases/proteases and solubilize enzymes.
Allow to cool, then supplement with 500 mM CaCl2 [200 uL] and BSA [10 mg].
Filter-sterilize the medium using a 0.45 µm PVDF membrane.

steps.title: Prepare 40% PEG-Calcium Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare the transfection solution (approx. 200 uL needed per transformation) fresh on the day of transfection.

substeps.instruction: Mix PEG-4000 [400 mg], 1 M Mannitol [200 uL], 500 mM CaCl2 [200 uL], and dd-H2O [600 uL] per 1 mL.
Mix until dissolved (approx. 1 hour).

steps.title: Prepare Cutting Tools
steps.instruction: Prepare a clean cutting board, tweezers, and a fresh, sharp razor or scalpel.

steps.title: Excise Plant Tissue
steps.instruction: Isolate tissue as early in the day as possible to limit starch accumulation; keep plants in the dark during isolation.

substeps.instruction: For Arabidopsis: Excise fully-expanded rosette leaves (typically leaves 4-7 from 3-week-old plants). Cut the mid-section into approx. 1-mm strips perpendicular to the midvein using a razor blade without crushing the tissue.

For Wheat: Excise the primary leaf of approx. 1-week-old plants. Lightly score the abaxial side and peel away the epidermis to expose the mesophyll. Place tissue strips mesophyll side down in 0.6 M mannitol for 15 minutes in the dark.
Immediately place Arabidopsis strips or transfer wheat peels into the enzyme solution, ensuring all cutting edges are exposed.

steps.title: Isolate Protoplasts
steps.instruction: Digest the tissue to release protoplasts.

substeps.instruction: Vacuum infiltrate for 30 minutes in a desiccator, then release pressure gently and evenly.
Incubate in the dark at 23 °C for ≥ 3 hours with gentle rotation (~40 rpm).
Centrifuge for 3 minutes at 80 rcf (soft ramp / brakes off).
Filter the solution through a 50 or 70 µm cell strainer into a falcon or round bottom centrifuge tube. Keep on ice and shielded from direct light.
Add an equal volume of W5 solution and mix with gentle swirling for 10 seconds until the solution turns green.

steps.title: Purify and Wash Protoplasts
steps.instruction: Clean the protoplast suspension to remove debris.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge for 3 minutes at 80 rcf (soft ramp / brakes off).
Remove the majority of the supernatant and resuspend protoplasts with gentle swirling.
Add half-volume W5 solution and rest on ice for ≤ 30 minutes.
Remove as much supernatant as possible without disturbing the pellet and add half-volume MMg solution.
Wash once more with an equal volume of W5 solution, centrifuge, and remove supernatant (resuspend by swirling before proceeding).

steps.title: Quantify Protoplast Density
steps.instruction: Determine the concentration of intact protoplasts using a haemocytometer and light microscope.

substeps.instruction: Load 10 μL of suspension and count intact, spherical protoplasts across 3-5 squares.
Calculate density: (number of protoplasts / number of squares) x 10^4 x Dilution Factor.
Optional: Add 0.1% (w/v) trypan blue and 10 μg/mL propidium iodide prior to counting to identify broken cells.
Check for lysed cells, free chlorophylls, and epidermal debris.
Supplement the protoplast solution with 10 μg/mL propidium iodide (λEx = 535 nm; λEm = 617 nm) using gentle flicking.
Measure fluorescence using a flow cytometer (e.g., BD FACS Aria II, Invitrogen Attune NxT) as soon as possible after staining.

steps.title: Prepare for Transformation
steps.instruction: Standardize the protoplast concentration and prepare tubes.

substeps.instruction: Adjust protoplast density to 3x10^5 protoplasts mL-1 MMg.
Prepare clean 2 mL microcentrifuge tubes and determine the plasmids to be transformed.

steps.title: Perform PEG-Mediated Transformation
steps.instruction: Transfect the protoplasts with plasmid DNA.

substeps.instruction: Incubate tubes for 5 to 15 minutes at 23 °C.
Add 10-20 μg of plasmid DNA (10-20 μL) into all tubes.

Quickly perform the following: (I) Add 30,000 - 60,000 protoplasts (100 - 200 μl of 3x10^5 protoplasts mL-1 MMg) and mix with gentle flicking; (II) Add an equal volume of 40% PEG-calcium solution and mix with gentle flicking.
Note: Maintain a ratio of 1 μg DNA : 3,000 protoplasts and minimize incubation time of protoplasts with DNA alone.

steps.title: Recover and Incubate Protoplasts
steps.instruction: Wash the transfected cells and move them to culture plates.

substeps.instruction: Add 2x volume of W5 solution (~840 μL) and mix by gentle inversion.
Centrifuge for 3 minutes at 80 rcf (soft ramp / brakes off).
Discard supernatant and resuspend protoplasts in culture plate wells with W5 or WI solution: 1 mL (6-well), 0.5 mL (12-well), or 0.25 mL (24-well).
Incubate protoplasts in the dark at 23 °C for 16-48 h.
